title: Binary 4-necklace fixed-point checks for Polya enumeration

problemStatement.formal: \sum_{r : \mathrm{Fin}\,4} 2^{\gcd(r,4)} = 24, so the cyclic Burnside count for binary necklaces of length 4 is 24/4 = 6.
problemStatement.plain: This entry verifies the fixed-point counts behind Burnside's lemma for binary 4-necklaces. The Lean proof checks each rotation, proves the Polya fixed-point sum, and records the divisor-sum form of the necklace formula.
whyMatters: Turns the abstract Burnside-counting story into a fully checked finite necklace example.
Provides a concrete axiom-free bridge from fixed-point counts to the Polya enumeration formula.

proven: `IsFixed` defines colorings fixed by a cyclic rotation.
`fixed_factors_through_mod` proves fixed colorings are constant on residue classes modulo the relevant gcd.
`polya_cyclic_fixed_count` proves the fixed-coloring count is k^gcd(r,n).
`fp_count_rot0_4_2`, `fp_count_rot1_4_2`, `fp_count_rot2_4_2`, and `fp_count_rot3_4_2` compute the four binary length-4 rotation counts.
open: The parent `BurnsideCounting.lean` still contains axiomatized Burnside infrastructure.
The Aristotle helper file linked nearby has sorries; the main OQ03 file used here is the clean source.
knownResults.goal: Keep this as the finite, computation-backed Polya example while future work connects it to the parent Burnside lemma without axioms.
